cues.en: Mike: So far in this section, I've focused on d-prime and response bias.
cues.zh: Mike：這一節到目前為止，我著重介紹 d′ 與反應偏誤。

cues.en: Those are two commonly used measures of binary classification results, so generating this table, this two-by-two table,
cues.zh: 這是兩種常用的二元分類結果指標，也就是產生這個表格、這個二乘二表格的結果，

cues.en: that we've been looking at in the past several videos.
cues.zh: 也就是前幾部影片一直在看的表格。

cues.en: Well, it turns out there are several more quantifications of binary classification data and in this video, I'm gonna focus on one of them, it's called F-score,
cues.zh: 其實，二元分類資料還有好幾種量化方式，這部影片我要介紹其中一種，叫做 F 分數，

cues.en: and there's gonna be also another couple of measures that I will introduce you to along the way.
cues.zh: 過程中也會順便介紹另外幾項指標。

cues.en: And when we switch to code in a few minutes, you will also see how the F-score is related to d-prime which we've already been working with.
cues.zh: 幾分鐘後進入程式時，你也會看到，F 分數與我們已經在使用的 d′ 有什麼關係。

cues.en: So let's go back to our friendly little two-by-two table here.
cues.zh: 回到我們熟悉的小小二乘二表格。

cues.en: So before defining F-score, I'm going to define two other variables that are actually used in computing the F-score and that's called precision and recall.
cues.zh: 在定義 F 分數之前，我先定義計算 F 分數會用到的另外兩個變數，稱為精確率與召回率。

cues.en: So precision is this very simple fraction here.
cues.zh: 精確率就是這裡這個非常簡單的分數。

cues.en: It is the number of hits divided by the number of hits plus the number of false alarms.
cues.zh: 命中次數除以命中次數加上誤報次數。

cues.en: So it's essentially just looking at the top row of this table here and one way to see this is that it's a normalized measure of the number of hits.
cues.zh: 基本上，就是看這個表格最上面那一列；可以把它視為命中次數的正規化指標。

cues.en: So you're normalizing, in this case, for the number of times that you said yes but that was actually just a guess and you got it wrong.
cues.zh: 這裡的正規化，考慮的是你回答「是」，但其實只是猜測，而且猜錯的次數。

cues.en: So precision is the number of hits normalizing for the marginal across your perception, and then we have recall and you can see the formula looks really similar.
cues.zh: 因此，精確率是命中次數，以你的感知這一側的邊際總數來正規化；接著是召回率，你可以看到公式很相似。

cues.en: We still have hits on the numerator and in the denominator, but here we are normalizing for misses instead of for just false alarms.
cues.zh: 分子與分母仍然都有命中，但這裡是用漏失來正規化，而不是只用誤報。

cues.en: So this way we can draw this.
cues.zh: 因此，我們可以這樣畫出來。

cues.en: This is now the column.
cues.zh: 現在看的是這一欄。

cues.en: So now we're looking at a normalized measure of hits, but now we're normalizing according to the marginal of reality, not according to the marginal of perception.
cues.zh: 因此，現在也是命中的正規化指標，但這次是依照真實情況的邊際總數，而不是感知的邊際總數來正規化。

cues.en: Okay, so with these two quantities in mind, we can now define the F-score.
cues.zh: 了解這兩個量之後，就可以定義 F 分數。

cues.en: Also called the F1 score, I'll get back to this number in a moment, and that is essentially the product of precision by recall divided by the sum of precision and recall.
cues.zh: 它也叫 F1 分數；稍後再談這個數字。基本上，它是精確率乘上召回率，再除以精確率與召回率的和。

cues.en: There's a little factor of two up here.
cues.zh: 上面還有一個小小的係數 2。

cues.en: Now it turns out that because precision and recall are both defined by other features, we can actually simplify this.
cues.zh: 因為精確率與召回率都是由其他量定義的，所以其實可以化簡。

cues.en: I'm not gonna go through all the math, so I'm skipping some of the intermediate algebraic steps here, but this ends up simplifying to the number of hits divided by the number of hits
cues.zh: 我不會完整推導數學，這裡跳過一些代數中間步驟，最後會化簡成命中次數除以命中次數

cues.en: plus the average of false alarms and misses.
cues.zh: 加上誤報與漏失的平均。

cues.en: So so if you would like, now if you want to, at the end of this video, you can go back to this and essentially to get from this expression to this expression,
cues.zh: 如果你願意，在這部影片結束後可以回頭看看；要從這個式子得到這個式子，

cues.en: all you have to do is substitute in for precision and recall, you substitute these values.
cues.zh: 只要把精確率與召回率代換成這些值。

cues.en: So yeah, you do this substitution, a little bit of algebraic simplification, and you should arrive at this fraction here.
cues.zh: 做這個代換，再稍微化簡代數，就應該得到這裡的分數。

cues.en: So this is pretty interesting.
cues.zh: 這很有意思。

cues.en: Hits are the ways of guessing correct and you said yes.
cues.zh: 命中是你猜對而且回答「是」的情況。

cues.en: Of course, you can also be correct and say no.
cues.zh: 當然，你也可能回答「否」而且答對。

cues.en: That would be a correct rejection that's not included in the F-score.
cues.zh: 那就是正確拒絕，它並沒有包含在 F 分數中。

cues.en: So it's the ways of being correct when you say yes, and then these are the two ways of making a mistake in the table.
cues.zh: 因此，這是回答「是」而答對的情況，而這兩個是表格中犯錯的兩種方式。

cues.en: These are the two types of errors in our binary classification.
cues.zh: 也就是二元分類中的兩種錯誤。

cues.en: So the false alarms plus the misses and we're just averaging those two together.
cues.zh: 誤報加上漏失，我們把這兩者取平均。

cues.en: So now let's think about how to interpret the F-score.
cues.zh: 現在想一想，要如何解讀 F 分數。

cues.en: Well, we want hits to be high, right?
cues.zh: 我們希望命中次數很高，對吧？

cues.en: That's what you want in a alternative force choice task.
cues.zh: 這是選項強迫選擇作業中想要的情況。

cues.en: You want the number of hits to be high.
cues.zh: 你希望命中次數很高。

cues.en: So let's think about how high the F-score possibly could be if there's an upper bound.
cues.zh: 因此，如果 F 分數有上限，它最高能到多少？

cues.en: Well, if the hits get larger and larger so you keep getting more and more hits, that doesn't really bring up the F-score so much because we also have the number of hits in the denominator.
cues.zh: 如果命中越來越多，不斷增加，其實不會讓 F 分數增加太多，因為分母也有命中次數。

cues.en: So then we can think about these two terms, the ways of making mistakes.
cues.zh: 接著，可以考慮這兩個項，也就是犯錯的方式。

cues.en: Now these two terms of course cannot be negative.
cues.zh: 當然，這兩個項不可能是負的。

cues.en: The smallest they can be a zero.
cues.zh: 最小只能是零。

cues.en: So if this term is zero here, then we just have hits divided by hits.
cues.zh: 因此，如果這一項是零，就只剩下命中除以命中。

cues.en: So the largest the F-score could possibly be is one.
cues.zh: 所以 F 分數最高只能是 1。

cues.en: You cannot have an F-score higher than one.
cues.zh: 不可能有高於 1 的 F 分數。

cues.en: And on the lower bound, we have an F-score of zero.
cues.zh: 至於下限，F 分數可以是零。

cues.en: If you have zero hits and so all incorrect responses, then you're gonna have zero divided by something.
cues.zh: 如果命中次數是零，也就是全都答錯，就會是零除以某個數。

cues.en: So the lowest the F-score can possibly be is zero, and then we can also think about what would be the middle range if you were just guessing.
cues.zh: 因此，F 分數最低只能是零；接著，也可以想一想，如果只是猜測，中間的值會是多少。

cues.en: Well, if you're just completely randomly guessing, you would expect the same number of trials to go in each of those four bins in our plots.
cues.zh: 如果完全隨機猜測，我們預期圖中這四個格子的試驗次數都相同。

cues.en: Let me go back to the previous slide.
cues.zh: 讓我回到上一張投影片。

cues.en: So if you're just guessing in an experiment, you're gonna have roughly equal numbers across these four table elements over here.
cues.zh: 如果在實驗中只是猜測，這四個表格元素中的次數大致會一樣。

cues.en: So that would mean, let's go with 10.
cues.zh: 那麼，就用 10 好了。

cues.en: Let's say there's 10 hits, 10 hits, 10 false alarms, and 10 misses.
cues.zh: 假設有 10 次命中、10 次命中、10 次誤報，以及 10 次漏失。

cues.en: So we have 10 divided by 10 plus.
cues.zh: 所以是 10 除以 10 加上……

cues.en: This would be 10 plus 10 divided by two is 20, so this would be 10 divided by 20 which is .5.
cues.zh: 這裡是 10 加 10 除以 2，得到 20，因此是 10 除以 20，也就是 0.5。

cues.en: So this tells us that an F-score of .5 corresponds to pure guessing.
cues.zh: 這表示 F 分數為 0.5，對應純粹猜測。

cues.en: So this is F-score or F1 score and it turns out that some people argue that in certain applications for certain kinds of experiments or certain kinds of data sets,
cues.zh: 這就是 F 分數或 F1 分數。有些人主張，對某些應用、某類實驗或某類資料集，

cues.en: you want to weight precision or recall relatively more, relatively less, so therefore you can change the weighting of these two variables and that will change this little number here.
cues.zh: 會希望相對提高或降低精確率或召回率的權重，因此可以改變這兩個變數的權重，這裡的小數字也會跟著改變。

cues.en: So you can have an F.5 score, for example, or an F2 score, an F4 score, and essentially it's following the same formula.
cues.zh: 例如可以有 F0.5 分數、F2 分數、F4 分數，基本上遵循相同的公式。

cues.en: You're just adding some weights.
cues.zh: 只是加入一些權重。

cues.en: So you could multiply precision by two and multiply recall by 1/2 and so on, so this is just the basic F1 score.
cues.zh: 例如把精確率乘以 2，召回率乘以 1/2 等等；這裡介紹的只是基本的 F1 分數。

cues.en: Okay, so now let's switch to code and continue exploring the F-score and the relationship between F-score and d-prime using my all time favorite method
cues.zh: 現在切換到程式，繼續探索 F 分數，以及 F 分數與 d′ 的關係，使用我最喜歡的方式，

cues.en: of understanding concept in statistics and math in general which is of course, you know, coding.
cues.zh: 來理解統計與一般數學概念；當然，就是寫程式。

cues.en: So that's what we're gonna do now.
cues.zh: 現在就來做。

cues.en: So here we are in MATLAB and we'll switch to Python in a small number of minutes.
cues.zh: 這裡是 MATLAB，再過幾分鐘會切換到 Python。

cues.en: So what we are going to do is run some experiments.
cues.zh: 我們要做的是跑一些實驗。

cues.en: We are going to simulate data in experiments and then compute these various measures like d-prime and F-score and a few others, I'll get to that in a moment,
cues.zh: 我們會模擬實驗資料，再計算 d′、F 分數和其他幾項指標；其他指標稍後再談，

cues.en: and then we can do some visualizations and yeah, it's gonna just clarify some points that were a little bit abstract in the slides.
cues.zh: 接著做一些視覺化，讓投影片中稍微抽象的部分更清楚。

cues.en: So we're gonna come up with experiments that have actually 100 trials.
cues.zh: 我們要建立的實驗，其實各有 100 次試驗。

cues.en: So it says N equals 50 here, but you'll see in the code in a moment this is gonna be times two for the number of total trials.
cues.zh: 雖然這裡寫 N 等於 50，但稍後會看到，程式中會乘以 2，才是總試驗次數。

cues.en: Then we are going to simulate 10,000 experiments.
cues.zh: 接著，我們要模擬 10,000 個實驗。

cues.en: We're gonna run this experiment 10,000 times and each experiment we get to compute d-prime and the F-score.
cues.zh: 把這個實驗跑 10,000 次，每個實驗都計算 d′ 與 F 分數。

cues.en: Okay, so here's the for loop that goes over the number of experiments, so let's see what we do inside each experiment.
cues.zh: 這個 for 迴圈會走過所有實驗，來看看每個實驗內做什麼。

cues.en: Well, the first thing we do is generate data.
cues.zh: 首先，產生資料。

cues.en: You can see here we are generating hits, misses, correct rejections, and false alarms, and these are defined according to some random integer
cues.zh: 你可以看到，我們產生命中、漏失、正確拒絕與誤報，而它們是根據一個隨機整數定義的，

cues.en: between one and N minus one, so between one and 49.
cues.zh: 範圍是 1 到 N−1，也就是 1 到 49。

cues.en: So that's the number of hits is gonna be, yeah, random number of hits.
cues.zh: 所以命中次數，就是隨機的命中次數。

cues.en: The number of misses is going to be, the total number of trials here divided by the number of hits, and then same story for correct rejections and false alarms.
cues.zh: 漏失次數則是這裡的總試驗次數除以命中次數；正確拒絕與誤報也是一樣的道理。

cues.en: Now you can see why these two sum up to N and these two sum up to N.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，這兩個加起來是 N，這兩個加起來也是 N。

cues.en: So that's why I specified N equals 50, but we actually got 100 trials in the experiment.
cues.zh: 因此，我設定 N 等於 50，但實驗中實際上有 100 次試驗。

cues.en: Okay, anyway so here we compute the F-score.
cues.zh: 接著在這裡計算 F 分數。

cues.en: You can see that's just a direct, easy implementation of the code, of the formula that I showed in the slide.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，只是把我在投影片中展示的公式，直接而簡單地實作成程式。

cues.en: So we have hits divided by hits plus the average of the two ways of making a mistake in the experiment.
cues.zh: 命中除以命中，加上實驗中兩種犯錯方式的平均。

cues.en: And here we have the formula for d-prime which now should look familiar to you.
cues.zh: 這裡是 d′ 的公式，現在看起來應該很熟悉。

cues.en: It's essentially the normalized number of hits or the proportion, I should say, of hits and the proportion of false alarms.
cues.zh: 基本上，就是正規化的命中次數，更精確地說是命中比例，以及誤報比例。

cues.en: Project those through the inverse of normal probability distribution and take their difference.
cues.zh: 將它們透過常態機率分布的反函數轉換，再取差。

cues.en: Now it turns out that there's going to be some variability.
cues.zh: 不過，兩者之間會有一些變異。

cues.en: There's gonna be some unaccounted for differences between d-prime and F-score and to understand that difference, we can additionally plot the specificity.
cues.zh: 在 d′ 與 F 分數之間，會有一些尚未解釋的差異；為了了解這種差異，還可以畫出特異度。

cues.en: Now specificity isn't a variable that I talked about in the slides, but you can see it's a marginal, normalized measure of the other way of getting correct responses.
cues.zh: 特異度是投影片裡沒有談到的變數，但你可以看到，它是另一種答對方式的邊際正規化指標。

cues.en: So you can get correct responses as hits and you can also have correct responses as correct rejections which is where you say no and the true answer was no.
cues.zh: 你可以透過命中答對，也可以透過正確拒絕答對，也就是你回答「否」，而真正的答案也是「否」。

cues.en: Okay, so we will get back to specificity in a moment.
cues.zh: 稍後會再回來談特異度。

cues.en: Here you can see I'm also computing or I've provided code for precision and recall.
cues.zh: 這裡你可以看到，我也計算了精確率與召回率，或說提供了它們的程式。

cues.en: So I'm not actually going to use this.
cues.zh: 我實際上不會使用它們。

cues.en: Here, you can see I'm also not storing these variables.
cues.zh: 這裡也可以看到，我沒有儲存這些變數。

cues.en: Here, I'm storing the d-prime specificity and F-score for every iteration, every run of the experiment.
cues.zh: 這裡則會在每次迭代、每次實驗中，儲存 d′、特異度與 F 分數。

cues.en: You can see I'm not doing that here.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，這裡沒有這樣做。

cues.en: I just provided this code in case you would like to continue exploring the relationship across these different variables.
cues.zh: 提供這段程式，只是讓你可以繼續探索這些不同變數之間的關係。

cues.en: Okay, so now let's plot them.
cues.zh: 現在來畫圖。

cues.en: So here I'm going to generate a plot of the d-primes by the F-scores and let's see what this scatter plot looks like.
cues.zh: 這裡我要產生 d′ 對 F 分數的圖，看看散佈圖會是什麼樣子。

cues.en: Okay, it looks like this.
cues.zh: 看起來是這樣。

cues.en: So we have d-primes on the x-axis and F-score on the y-axis, and it's like this beautiful waterfall pattern or something.
cues.zh: X 軸是 d′，Y 軸是 F 分數，像是一種美麗的瀑布圖案。

cues.en: But before that, I just wanna talk about each of these variables individually.
cues.zh: 但在那之前，我先分別談談這些變數。

cues.en: So you can see that d-prime goes from minus, a little over minus .4 up to .4, a little above.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，d′ 從略低於負 0.4，到略高於正 0.4。

cues.en: Four, sorry, not .4.
cues.zh: 是 4，抱歉，不是 0.4。

cues.en: So it goes from around minus four to plus four and that's to be expected for random d-prime values.
cues.zh: 所以範圍約從負 4 到正 4，這是隨機 d′ 值的預期情況。

cues.en: You can also see that the distribution of d-prime is clustered around zero.
cues.zh: 你也可以看到，d′ 的分布聚集在零附近。

cues.en: That's also to be expected because a d-prime of zero corresponds to random guessing and that's basically what we're simulating in this experiment.
cues.zh: 這也符合預期，因為 d′ 為零對應隨機猜測，而這基本上就是這個實驗模擬的情況。

cues.en: This is just pure random guessing, okay?
cues.zh: 這完全只是隨機猜測。

cues.en: And then on the y-axis you can see that the F-scores range from zero up to one.
cues.zh: 在 Y 軸，你可以看到 F 分數介於零到 1 之間。

cues.en: That's also, as I showed in these slides, it actually doesn't get exactly to zero and it doesn't get exactly to one.
cues.zh: 這也是投影片中展示過的；不過，實際上不會恰好等於零，也不會恰好等於 1。

cues.en: And I would like you to look at the code, the way we simulate the experiment, to understand why, the way that I've written the code,
cues.zh: 我希望你看看程式，看看我們如何模擬實驗，了解為什麼以我寫程式的方式，

cues.en: we never get an F-score of exactly zero or exactly one.
cues.zh: 永遠不會得到恰好為零或恰好為 1 的 F 分數。

cues.en: And you can also see.
cues.zh: 你也可以看到，

cues.en: Here, I've drawn a horizontal line at an F-score of .5.
cues.zh: 這裡我在 F 分數 0.5 畫了一條水平線。

cues.en: You can see that the data are centered at .5.
cues.zh: 資料以 0.5 為中心。

cues.en: Again, that's to be expected because these are random data.
cues.zh: 這也符合預期，因為資料是隨機的。

cues.en: So over the course of many, many, many experiments, we expect the F-score to be, the average F-score over all these experiments to be .5.
cues.zh: 因此，經過許多、許多次實驗，我們預期所有這些實驗的平均 F 分數是 0.5。

cues.en: All right, very good.
cues.zh: 很好。

cues.en: So now you can see that d-prime and F-score, if we compute the linear correlation, they're correlated at .85 so they're already pretty strongly related to each other.
cues.zh: 現在你可以看到，若計算 d′ 與 F 分數的線性相關，相關係數是 0.85，兩者已經有相當強的關係。

cues.en: But it looks like there's these separate ways of them being related to each other and it turns out that the key difference is the normalization of F-score
cues.zh: 但它們似乎還有幾種不同的關聯方式；關鍵差別在於 F 分數的正規化方式，

cues.en: versus the normalization of d-prime.
cues.zh: 與 d′ 的正規化方式不同。

cues.en: So to understand this a little bit better, I'm going to plot the color, so I'm gonna make the color of the scatters not be black which they are specified here.
cues.zh: 為了更了解這點，我要改變散佈點的顏色；不再使用這裡指定的黑色。

cues.en: Instead I'm gonna specify that the color should be the variable specificity.
cues.zh: 改成指定用特異度這個變數作為顏色。

cues.en: So now let's rerun the code and now this, visually, first of all, it looks really nice, but you can see now specificity actually corresponds to the color value.
cues.zh: 重新執行程式；首先，這在視覺上很漂亮，而現在特異度對應的是顏色值。

cues.en: So these are all the experiments that had very low specificity.
cues.zh: 這些都是特異度很低的實驗。

cues.en: These are the experiments that had very high specificity, again, just to make this a little bit more concrete.
cues.zh: 這些是特異度很高的實驗；再說得具體一點，

cues.en: So specificity is basically the number of correct rejections, it's normalized, but you can think of a high score.
cues.zh: 特異度基本上是正確拒絕的次數，雖然它經過正規化，但你可以把高分想成，

cues.en: So here, red colors indicating a lot of correct rejections and a low score indicating low correct rejections.
cues.zh: 這裡的紅色代表許多正確拒絕，低分代表較少的正確拒絕。

cues.en: So you can see that the relationship between d-prime and F-score is not really trivial or it's not so straightforward.
cues.zh: 因此，d′ 與 F 分數的關係，並不是那麼簡單或直接。

cues.en: It's two dimensional relationship.
cues.zh: 這是一個二維關係。

cues.en: We also have to incorporate some of the other things that are happening in this experiment and that's essentially because of the normalization.
cues.zh: 還必須納入這個實驗中發生的其他事情，基本上是正規化造成的。

cues.en: For example, the number of correct rejections or the proportion of correct rejections is actually implicitly incorporated here into this subtractive term in d-prime
cues.zh: 例如，正確拒絕的次數，或正確拒絕的比例，其實隱含在 d′ 這個相減的項裡，

cues.en: and that's because the correct rejection is the inverse of the false alarm rate.
cues.zh: 因為正確拒絕與誤報率是相反的。

cues.en: So these two are related to each other and that's why incorporating this measure of specificity helps us understand the relationship between d-prime and F-score.
cues.zh: 因此，兩者彼此相關，納入特異度這個指標，就能幫助理解 d′ 與 F 分數的關係。

cues.en: Nonetheless there is a more generic relationship between d-prime and F-score which is that you want both of those measures to be high.
cues.zh: 不過，d′ 與 F 分數還有一個比較一般的關係，就是你希望這兩項指標都很高。

cues.en: You want them to be relatively high.
cues.zh: 你希望它們相對較高。

cues.en: That indicates better performance.
cues.zh: 那表示表現比較好。

cues.en: Okay, so let's start by importing some of the modules that we will need here, some of these libraries, and what we are going to do is run through a bunch of experiments.
cues.zh: 先匯入這裡會用到的模組與函式庫，接著跑一大批實驗。

cues.en: In fact, we're going to repeat this experiment 10,000 times and we're going to simulate data from 100 trials.
cues.zh: 我們會把這個實驗重複 10,000 次，並模擬 100 次試驗的資料。

cues.en: This actually says N equals 50, but you'll see in a moment that the number of trials in each of these 10,000 experiments is actually two times 50.
cues.zh: 這裡其實寫 N 等於 50，但稍後會看到，這 10,000 個實驗中，每個實驗的試驗次數都是 2 乘以 50。

cues.en: Okay, so here we have a for loop over our experiments.
cues.zh: 這裡是走過所有實驗的 for 迴圈。

cues.en: So everything that's inside this for loop is what takes place inside one simulated experiment.
cues.zh: 因此，這個 for 迴圈裡的所有操作，都是在一個模擬實驗內進行。

cues.en: So what we do, first of all, is generate the data.
cues.zh: 首先要產生資料。

cues.en: So here we have hits, misses, correct rejections, and false alarms and you can see the way that I'm generating these data randomly is by coming up with,
cues.zh: 這裡有命中、漏失、正確拒絕與誤報；你可以看到，我隨機產生這些資料的方式是

cues.en: drawing some random integer between one and 49.
cues.zh: 抽取一個介於 1 到 49 之間的隨機整數。

cues.en: Remember this is exclusive, so this is gonna be number of hits corresponding to one and 49, and then we define the number of misses as the number of hits
cues.zh: 記得，上界不包含在內，所以命中次數會介於 1 到 49；接著把漏失次數定義為命中次數，

cues.en: or yeah, the total N minus the number of hits.
cues.zh: 或者說，總數 N 減去命中次數。

cues.en: So I'm defining these to be complimentary here and same story for correct rejections and false alarms.
cues.zh: 所以我在這裡把兩者定義成互補；正確拒絕與誤報也是同樣的道理。

cues.en: So you can see these two numbers will add up to 50, these two will add up to 50, and that's why there's 100 trials in total.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，這兩個數字相加是 50，這兩個相加也是 50，所以總共有 100 次試驗。

cues.en: Now of course, this is just random, so we do expect some diversity across the different experiments because of sampling variability, just picking random numbers,
cues.zh: 當然，這是隨機的，所以不同實驗之間會因抽樣變異、隨機抽數字，而有一些差異，

cues.en: but we also expect any measure like d-prime or F-score, over 10,000 repeats of this experiment, we expect those measures to converge
cues.zh: 但我們也預期，經過 10,000 次實驗重複後，d′、F 分數這類指標會收斂

cues.en: to a value of randomness, whatever corresponds to random in the F-score and d-prime, and we'll talk about that in a moment when we look at the graph.
cues.zh: 到代表隨機狀態的值，也就是 F 分數與 d′ 各自對應隨機的值；稍後看圖時再談。

cues.en: Okay, so here we are computing F-score.
cues.zh: 這裡計算 F 分數。

cues.en: You can see we're saving the F-score for each run this iteration loop, this experiment loop.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，每次跑這個迭代迴圈、這個實驗迴圈時，都會儲存 F 分數。

cues.en: And this is just the simple implementation of the formula that I showed in the slide.
cues.zh: 這只是把投影片中的公式簡單地實作出來。

cues.en: So hits divided by hits plus the average of the two ways of making mistakes in the experiment, so false alarms plus misses.
cues.zh: 命中除以命中，加上實驗中兩種犯錯方式的平均，也就是誤報加漏失的平均。

cues.en: Here we have a variable called specificity which I didn't really talk about in the slides, but you can see it's similar to precision and accuracy
cues.zh: 這裡有一個叫做特異度的變數，投影片中沒有特別談到，但可以看到，它與精確率和準確率類似，

cues.en: so it's a normalized way of looking at correct rejections.
cues.zh: 是經過正規化、用來看正確拒絕的方式。

cues.en: So correct rejections divided by the sum or the marginal of correct rejections and false alarms.
cues.zh: 也就是正確拒絕除以正確拒絕與誤報的和，也就是邊際總數。

cues.en: So essentially it's the correct rejections or saying no when, so correctly saying no when there really was no stimulus present, there was no light flickering that was there,
cues.zh: 基本上，是正確拒絕，也就是實際上沒有刺激存在、沒有閃光時，正確回答「否」，

cues.en: normalized by the column margin across the times when the actual stimulus was really absent.
cues.zh: 再用實際刺激確實不存在時，那一欄的邊際總數來正規化。

cues.en: Okay, and then we have d-prime.
cues.zh: 接著是 d′。

cues.en: This should look familiar.
cues.zh: 這應該很熟悉。

cues.en: You've seen this a couple videos ago.
cues.zh: 幾部影片之前你已經看過。

cues.en: It's essentially the proportion of hits minus the proportion of false alarms, but then those proportions are projected through the inverse probability,
cues.zh: 基本上，是命中比例減去誤報比例，只不過要先讓這些比例經過反機率，

cues.en: inverse normal probability distribution.
cues.zh: 也就是反常態機率分布的轉換。

cues.en: And now here we have the other two variables that I introduced in the slide, precision and recall.
cues.zh: 這裡則是投影片中介紹的另外兩個變數，精確率與召回率。

cues.en: You can see these are not used here.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，這裡沒有使用它們。

cues.en: I'm not storing these for each run through the experiment.
cues.zh: 我沒有在每次實驗迴圈時儲存它們。

cues.en: I'm just including the variables here, partly just so you can see how easy it is to implement them.
cues.zh: 把這些變數放在這裡，一部分是為了讓你看到實作有多簡單。

cues.en: But also it's a little bit of an encouragement for you to play around with this code and explore these concepts and these measures of these
cues.zh: 另一部分也是鼓勵你自己玩玩這段程式，探索這些概念，以及這些

cues.en: two alternative forced choice experiments on your own if you like.
cues.zh: 二選一強迫選擇實驗的各項指標。

cues.en: Okay, so run through all this code and we don't get any errors or anything, so that's a good sign, and here's where the plotting comes in.
cues.zh: 執行整段程式，沒有任何錯誤，這是好現象；接下來是畫圖。

cues.en: So what we are going to do is plot d-prime, so a scatter plot of the d-primes by the F-scores over all of the different experiments.
cues.zh: 我們要畫出 d′，也就是所有不同實驗中，d′ 對 F 分數的散佈圖。

cues.en: So it looks like this.
cues.zh: 看起來是這樣。

cues.en: So it's a pretty neat looking, it looks like some digitized waterfall or something.
cues.zh: 這張圖很有意思，像是數位化的瀑布。

cues.en: So before talking about the relationship between d-prime and F-score, let me just quickly discuss each of these measures alone.
cues.zh: 在談 d′ 與 F 分數的關係之前，先簡單分別談談這兩項指標。

cues.en: So we can see the range of the d-prime values is somewhere around minus four to somewhere around plus four and the average, you can see,
cues.zh: 可以看到，d′ 的範圍大約從負 4 到正 4；至於平均值，你可以看到，

cues.en: they're all clustering around zero and that's of course, expected because these are just random data.
cues.zh: 它們都聚集在零附近，這當然符合預期，因為這些只是隨機資料。

cues.en: So it's no surprise that across 10,000 experiments, the data, the d-primes converge to zero.
cues.zh: 因此，在 10,000 個實驗中，資料，也就是 d′，收斂到零並不意外。

cues.en: Now here on the y-axis, we have F-score and you can see that they range from zero to one.
cues.zh: Y 軸這裡是 F 分數，你可以看到它們的範圍是零到 1。

cues.en: But in fact they, so it's not actually obvious from this plot, but it turns out that you can never get an F-score of exactly one and you don't get an F-score of exactly zero.
cues.zh: 但其實，從這張圖不容易看出來，你永遠不會得到恰好為 1 或恰好為零的 F 分數。

cues.en: Now in theory you can get F-scores of zero and one, but the way I have simulated the code or the way I've simulated the experiment, you don't actually get an F-score
cues.zh: 理論上當然可以有零與 1 的 F 分數，但以我模擬程式、或說模擬實驗的方式，實際上不會得到

cues.en: of absolute zero or absolute one.
cues.zh: 完全等於零或完全等於 1 的 F 分數。

cues.en: And I encourage you to take a moment and look at this code and make sure you understand why we don't get an F-score of exactly zero and one.
cues.zh: 我鼓勵你花點時間看程式，確認自己了解為什麼不會得到恰好為零與 1 的 F 分數。

cues.en: And of course, also you see there's this horizontal line at .5.
cues.zh: 當然，你也看到這條位於 0.5 的水平線。

cues.en: This corresponds to an F-score of chance as I explained in the slides so, and you can also see that the data are distributed, looks like they're roughly distributed around .5,
cues.zh: 就像投影片中解釋的，這對應機率水準的 F 分數；而你也可以看到，資料似乎大致分布在 0.5 附近，

cues.en: so the expected value, the average, is converging to .5.
cues.zh: 所以期望值，也就是平均值，會收斂到 0.5。

cues.en: Now here I've computed the linear correlation between these two measures.
cues.zh: 這裡我計算了兩項指標之間的線性相關。

cues.en: So they're clearly strongly related to each other, linearly related to each other, but you can also see that there's more going on between d-prime
cues.zh: 因此，它們顯然有很強的關係、很強的線性關係，但你也可以看到，d′

cues.en: and F-score than just a pure linear measure.
cues.zh: 與 F 分數之間，還有純粹線性指標以外的情況。

cues.en: Now part of that is because d-prime gets pushed through this probability distribution, so that stretches out the values at the low end and it stretches out the values at the high end,
cues.zh: 部分原因是 d′ 經過這個機率分布轉換，所以低端數值被拉開，高端數值也被拉開，

cues.en: but that doesn't really explain everything.
cues.zh: 但這無法解釋所有事情。

cues.en: In fact, what you see here is it looks like there's a bunch of different sigmoids showing this relationship, right?
cues.zh: 事實上，你看到的似乎是好幾條不同的 S 形曲線，顯示這種關係，對吧？

cues.en: So here is a sigmoidal relationship, so it's like there's a bunch of columns in here that relate F to d-prime according to some other variable.
cues.zh: 這裡是一條 S 形關係；所以這裡像有許多直條，依照另一個變數，連結 F 與 d′。

cues.en: So that turns out to be the case and that's why I've included this measure of specificity here.
cues.zh: 實際上確實如此，這也是我在這裡加入特異度指標的原因。

cues.en: Now the thing is that although d-prime includes, it looks like it's just including hits and false alarms, implicitly we're also including the other two categories,
cues.zh: 雖然 d′ 看起來只包含命中與誤報，但其實也隱含其他兩種類別，

cues.en: so correct rejections and misses in here.
cues.zh: 也就是這裡的正確拒絕與漏失。

cues.en: And that's because those two ways of saying no, correct rejections and misses, those are implicitly in here because we have the proportions of saying yes in here.
cues.zh: 因為我們在這裡用了回答「是」的比例，所以回答「否」的兩種方式，也就是正確拒絕與漏失，也隱含在裡面。

cues.en: Okay, so what I'm going to do now is color code all of these dots according to their specificity, so the c= gives us the color.
cues.zh: 現在我要依照特異度，對所有這些點進行顏色編碼，c= 就是設定顏色。

cues.en: So let's see what that looks like and first of all, it looks really beautiful, right?
cues.zh: 看看會變成什麼樣子；首先，看起來真的很漂亮，對吧？

cues.en: I hope you agree.
cues.zh: 希望你也同意。

cues.en: It's just very nice to look at.
cues.zh: 就是很好看。

cues.en: There's some missing points in here, of course.
cues.zh: 當然，這裡有一些缺少的點。

cues.en: Because we are just simulating random experiments, we're gonna be missing a couple of values here just by chance.
cues.zh: 因為我們只是模擬隨機實驗，所以會因為偶然因素而少掉幾個值。

cues.en: Okay, but what you see is that each of these columns seems to correspond to a particular color.
cues.zh: 不過，你會看到，每一條直條似乎都對應一種特定顏色。

cues.en: So these colors are reflecting essentially the normalized number of correct rejections.
cues.zh: 這些顏色基本上反映正規化後的正確拒絕次數。

cues.en: So this kind of deep purplish color here corresponds to very few correct rejections and getting up to yellow here corresponds to many correct rejections.
cues.zh: 因此，這種深紫色對應很少的正確拒絕，而這裡的黃色對應許多正確拒絕。

cues.en: So the relationship between d-prime and F-score is actually not just a two-dimensional relationship because of the way that the F-score and the d-prime are normalizing
cues.zh: 所以，d′ 與 F 分數的關係，其實不只是一個二維關係，因為 F 分數與 d′

cues.en: these variables in different ways.
cues.zh: 是以不同方式正規化這些變數。

cues.en: Okay, but all that said, there's clearly a consistency between the interpretation of d-prime and the interpretation of F-score which is that both of them should be higher.
cues.zh: 不過，話說回來，d′ 與 F 分數的解讀顯然有一致之處，就是兩者都應該越高越好。

cues.en: You want both of them to be higher and that indicates better performance.
cues.zh: 你希望兩者都比較高，那表示表現比較好。

cues.en: In this video, I introduced you to F-score and a couple of other measures like precision, and recall, and specificity, and we talked about the formula
cues.zh: 這部影片中，我介紹了 F 分數，以及精確率、召回率與特異度等其他指標，也談了公式，

cues.en: and we saw a nice example of how just looking at a formula for a variable tells us how to interpret that variable.
cues.zh: 並看到一個很好的例子：只要看看變數的公式，就能知道如何解讀這個變數。

cues.en: And then in the code, we explored F-score and its relationship to d-prime and you can see that it's actually quite a bit of complexity that comes out of these fairly simple binary classification experiments.
cues.zh: 接著透過程式，探索 F 分數及其與 d′ 的關係；你可以看到，這些相當簡單的二元分類實驗，其實能產生相當複雜的情況。

cues.en: So F-score and d-prime are closely related to each other, but to really appreciate that relationship, you also need to incorporate some additional measures.
cues.zh: 因此，F 分數與 d′ 關係密切，但要充分理解這種關係，也必須納入其他一些指標。
